SECTION: FMRT01 §3-§4 — design selection and exact sample size, decided before any world exists

PLANNING_INPUTS.late_trigger_loss: 0 of 53 FDFLT01 maturation events fell after step 10750 (max observed t_m = 9464), so the latest-allowed-trigger rule costs nothing

DESIGNS_COMPARED.causal_contrast: matched — the three arms are bit-identical immediately before the intervention, by construction
DESIGNS_COMPARED.note: one trajectory per block is forked at the trigger, so the pre-intervention matching gate is satisfied exactly rather than approximately

DESIGNS_COMPARED.causal_contrast: unmatched — arms differ by seed as well as by treatment

SELECTION_REASONING: A reaches the 0.80 power target at q = 0.40 with 150 primary worlds where B needs 256, and it delivers a strictly stronger causal contrast because the arms share the exact pre-intervention state. B was not retained merely because SPOIQ01 proposed it.

OPERATING_POINT.why_not_the_minimum_50: the comparison criterion is which DESIGN needs fewer worlds; within the chosen design the budget is then spent on power against a more conservative alternative

METHOD: exact binomial throughout, integrating over the random number of trigger-eligible worlds; no normal approximation

PRIMARY_NULL.WHY_0.05_IS_NOT_ARBITRARY: the frozen R2 material criterion D compares the daughter's post-intervention local X against the exact 95 per cent binomial upper bound on how much pre-intervention X could survive T_HOLD steps with no new production. Under NO_NEW_DAUGHTER_X_PRODUCTION the false-positive probability of criterion D is therefore bounded by 0.05 by construction. The null is the criterion's own false-positive rate, not a chosen number.
PRIMARY_NULL.critical_function: critical(M) = smallest k with P[Binomial(M,0.05) >= k] <= 0.05
